items.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998
items.q: Then John Williams comes aboard... Well you know you can’t come to — you can’t come to New York that way... And he, well I think within the next couple of days... he told Boston he’d never play

ctx.x: The pops orchestra thing, did you spot a need for that?

No. I didn’t know what else to do. There was no more studio. I didn’t fit anyplace. I’m not much of a rocker, and I guess then what I began with was my, I don’t know, stuck in my craw, something so-called I mean — forgive me — legitimate schooling, which is still very important. There was a man who ran Carnegie Hall called Sy Rosen. And after I had my catastrophe when Lenny Bernstein had the Philharmonic and I had this two week train wreck of all time, I recorded with that orchestra. They’re still buried in a…

of music. Well you know you can’t come to — you can but you can’t — you can’t come to New York that way, you know what I’m saying? And I think he thought that he’d come in there with the Boston Pops and he would just absolutely turn everything over. Well the press just crucified him, as they have all of us at one time or another. And he, well I think within the next couple of days, I don’t remember exactly, but he told Boston he’d never play, take the date off the schedule. And the day that call came to Carnegie,…
